Chapter 125: Sanguosha Will Soon Begin Charging

Young people, full of vigor, had really worn themselves out last night.

It was almost noon, and they were still lazing in bed, unwilling to get up.

Chen Guiliang wanted to keep sleeping too, but slacking off for half the day was his limit.

He got up and pulled open the curtains, exclaiming, "Wow, it's snowing so hard."

Bian Guanyue immediately perked up, threw on two layers of clothes, and climbed out of bed, excitedly watching the heavy snow drift outside the window.

The two of them just stood there by the window, arms around each other, chatting while they watched the snow.

After standing foolishly for half the day, they finally got dressed and went downstairs to find a place to eat nearby.

Once their stomachs were full, Chen Guiliang hailed a cab to take her to Wudaokou to catch the subway.

Bian Guanyue rolled down the car window, holding out her palm to catch the snowflakes. "This snow is so beautiful."

The taxi driver couldn't help but remind her, "Miss, maybe you should close the window?"

"Sorry about that." Bian Guanyue secretly made a face at Chen Guiliang. She was becoming more and more lively around her boyfriend.

Chen Guiliang whispered in her ear, "I'll build a snowman with you again next week."

"Mhm," Bian Guanyue nodded.

When they were near the subway station, Bian Guanyue was still a bit reluctant to part. Chen Guiliang had to coax her for a bit before she got out of the car.

"Driver, to the Peking University Science Park," Chen Guiliang said.

The driver stepped on the gas and said, "Young man, are you a Beida returnee?"

"How did you know?" Chen Guiliang asked.

The driver said, "I just dropped off a passenger last time who was a Peking University alumnus returned from studying abroad, starting a company in the Peking University Science Park. Your girlfriend's a graduate student, right?"

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Driver, you have sharp eyes."

"Heh, I've seen this plenty of times," the driver said smugly. "You two definitely started dating as undergraduates. You went abroad to study, your girlfriend stayed in the country for grad school, and you picked things back up when you returned."

"How about you tell me about the situation in Iraq instead?"

"Now that's something I know about, you've really asked the right person..."

After a round of idle chatter, Chen Guiliang arrived back at the company.

Ao Yanchen pulled him outside to talk. "You're quite the carefree hands-off boss."

"I've troubled you, Shijie," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

Ao Yanchen said, "About UnionPay, I've scheduled a meeting for you for next Monday. I also invited an alumnus who works at a law firm to help you discuss the specific contract details and supplementary clauses. His name is Zhou Yingzhuo, a graduate of Beida's Law Department. His fees are quite expensive. I hyped our company up to high heaven, saying that if this goes smoothly, we'll have a long-term partnership. Only then did he agree to a fifty percent discount to help out."

"Shijie, you're always so reliable!" Chen Guiliang said happily.

UnionPay's headquarters were in Shanghai, but they had an office here in Beijing.

As long as they settled the online banking payment system with UnionPay, they wouldn't need to negotiate with any of the other banks that supported UnionPay cards.

Ao Yanchen said, "The company is about to get on the right track. We'll need to hire a cashier and someone to manage the Taobao store."

"You can be in charge of that," Chen Guiliang said.

Ao Yanchen sighed. "I'm just fated to work hard. Ten thousand sets of the physical Sanguosha cards have been printed. They'll be shipped to the warehouse tonight."

From the previous 5,000 sets of Sanguosha, after subtracting the ones Chen Guiliang gave away and all the miscellaneous costs, they had only made a total profit of just over 30,000 yuan. The profit margin would definitely be higher from now on, and sales would primarily shift to the online store, with offline sales limited to a few surrounding universities.

That afternoon, Chen Guiliang called Zhou Yingzhuo, the senior alumnus who worked at the law firm.

After listening to Chen Guiliang's explanation, Zhou Yingzhuo said, "China UnionPay Electronic Payment was only established two years ago. They're still in their business development phase, so when you negotiate, you might as well try to push the price down a bit."

"I've asked around for you. The transaction fee for the gaming industry is generally between 0.6% and 1.2%. With a large volume, it can even drop below 0.5%. Prepare more materials and try to boast about your company's prospects. The larger your company's user base, the lower the transaction fee you can negotiate."

"There's also the settlement period and the security deposit. You're a small company, so you definitely can't avoid the deposit. I estimate you can negotiate it down to around 100,000 yuan. For the settlement period, aim for T+1. If they really won't budge, agree to T+3, but use it as an opportunity to demand a lower transaction fee."

"This visit of yours will be an initial discussion. You'll still need to pass their review before you can sign an agreement. I won't go with you this time; I'll show up on the day you sign. The liability for breach of contract is all standardized. I'll be responsible for negotiating the supplementary clauses then, such as the bank's responsibility in handling transaction disputes."

Chen Guiliang held a pen, quickly jotting down the key points.

This lawyer's fee was well worth it.

On Monday, Chen Guiliang took a taxi to the UnionPay Beijing office.

The person who received him was an account manager from the merchant services department.

"My surname is Qi, Qi Tao."

"Hello, Manager Qi. My name is Chen Guiliang. Here's my business card."

"Please, have a seat inside. Did you bring the documents?"

"I did."

Chen Guiliang took out a large pile of documents.

Although a version number wasn't required to operate a game at this time, the game still had to be registered. An ICP license and an Online Culture Operation Permit were also mandatory.

Manager Qi quickly leafed through the various documents and then asked about Sanguosha's situation.

Chen Guiliang produced a stack of data. "We sold 5,000 sets of physical Sanguosha cards in just two months. Moreover, our online store business has surged recently, and we've already printed another thirty thousand sets. The online version of Sanguosha is still in open beta, but it has gained nearly 15,000 users in less than a month, and the growth rate of registered users is getting faster and faster. We also operate the Sanguosha Tieba, which has already broken into the top 50 forums nationwide... Sanguosha is an online game with very promising prospects..."

"Card and board games have always had very low payment conversion rates," Manager Qi said. "For those who run card and board game platforms, our long-standing rule is to freeze a portion of the security deposit or extend the settlement period."

Chen Guiliang then took out a proposal for their payment model. "Although Sanguosha is also a card and board game, our payment model is different. We will continuously release new heroes, and players will need to spend money to play as them. In addition, we also sell card backgrounds, room backgrounds, hero skins, game items, and so on."

Manager Qi took it and examined it carefully.

Chen Guiliang continued to produce materials, but this time about Xiaonei. "Does Manager Qi know of Facebook?"

"I've heard of it," Manager Qi said, though he actually hadn't.

Chen Guiliang said, "It's an American internet company. It was founded less than a year ago and has already received angel investment and attracted the interest of multiple venture capital firms. My Xiaonei is benchmarked against Facebook, and it currently has no competitors in China. The Campus Belle Contest I organized has been reported by dozens of media outlets and even caused a sensation online for a time. Now, Xiaonei's registered users are growing rapidly, and venture capital will definitely come in next year."

Chen Guiliang even took out a stack of newspapers.

Manager Qi spent a long time reading through all the materials. "I remember Sohu has a 'Classmate Directory'."

"The 'Classmate Directory' has been dead in the water for a long time, and its users are constantly leaving," Chen Guiliang said. "Sohu's Classmate Directory is a Web 1.0 website, an outdated product. My Xiaonei is a Web 2.0 product, which is precisely the type that global capital is most willing to invest in right now."

The Web 2.0 hype had already started in China. Manager Qi had heard the term thrown around constantly, and his opinion of Chen Guiliang instantly rose.

Chen Guiliang continued, "If Sanguosha can partner with you, Manager Qi, Xiaonei will also interface with you in the future."

The emphasis of that sentence was on partnering with Manager Qi, not with UnionPay.

Manager Qi understood the unspoken meaning. He picked up the newspapers again and carefully read the reports on Chen Guiliang and Xiaonei.

He decided it was worth giving him a boost and making a friend out of Chen Guiliang.
